title: Marrowbridge University: who lost the Fall 2026 first-year class?
setting: Marrowbridge University is a fictional private university that enrols about 2,000 first-year students a year through two admission rounds: early action (EA) and regular decision (RD). In January 2026 the Admissions Office moved from its legacy system to a new application portal from Quillstone Systems. In October 2025 the Board's finance committee approved a revised merit scholarship schedule for students entering in Fall 2026. First-year enrolment for Fall 2026 came in well below the previous year, and the provost holds the Admissions Office responsible.
presentingRequest: The president asks you to assess whether the Admissions Office is responsible for the fall in first-year enrolment and what the university should do before next cycle's admission and award letters go out. You may collect at most two items from the catalogue.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Provost Daniel Arvidsson to the President, 2 Oct 2026
initialEvidence.text: Subject: Fall intake. We closed first-year enrolment at 1,810, down from 2,140 last fall. That is 330 fewer students and a serious hole in the tuition budget for four years. I've read the counsellor complaints. The January switch to the Quillstone portal was badly managed, regular-decision answers went out weeks late, and families noticed. I don't think we can go into the next cycle with the same leadership in Admissions. I'd like your support to make a change in the director role before autumn recruitment travel begins.

initialEvidence.source: Admissions operations dashboard, entering classes Fall 2025 vs Fall 2026, extracted 28 Sep 2026
initialEvidence.text: Completed applications: 9,850 → 10,240. Admits: 5,120 → 5,270. Admit rate: 52.0% → 51.5%. Mean admitted high-school GPA: 3.61 → 3.63. Enrolled first-years (census): 2,140 → 1,810. Yield (enrolled ÷ admits): 41.8% → 34.3%. Early action: deadline 1 Nov; decisions released 15 Dec in both years, processed on the legacy system. Regular decision: deadline 15 Jan; median days from complete file to decision 17 → 31 (2026 processed on Quillstone, live from 6 Jan). Enrolment deposit deadline: 1 May in both years.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Gareth Pell, college counsellor at Westcombe High School, to the Admissions Office, 20 Mar 2026
initialEvidence.text: Three of my students now have transcripts showing as 'missing' on your new portal, even though I uploaded them in early January and have the confirmation screens. One of them is a strong student. She was finally admitted with a merit award in mid-March, after weeks of waiting for a regular-decision answer, and she has now committed to another university because, in her words, 'they actually wanted me.' I have been sending students to Marrowbridge for twelve years, and this is the worst service I have seen.

initialEvidence.source: Chief of staff's notes from an interview with Director of Admissions Renata Solberg, 6 Oct 2026
initialEvidence.text: Solberg accepts that regular-decision answers were slow. Merit-eligible files (candidates for Dean's or Merit awards) go through a scholarship-scoring step run by the merit-review team. That team fell from six readers to four when two posts were frozen in December, and the Quillstone scoring module was also late and unstable. 'Both happened at once; nobody has measured which mattered more.' Presidential candidates are scored off-system by the honours committee, and files not eligible for merit review skip the step, so those decisions 'went out on time.' On the missing transcripts: 'I'm told by the team every file was complete before review; the status page lagged.' She calls the yield drop 'a market thing' and says no one has looked at it by segment.

initialEvidence.source: Minutes of the Board finance committee, 14 Oct 2025, item 6
initialEvidence.text: Undergraduate discount rate. The committee noted that the first-year institutional discount rate of 47% was above the peer median. Approved: a rebalanced merit scholarship schedule for Fall 2026 entrants, with Presidential awards unchanged; need-based grant policy unchanged. Projected effect: net tuition revenue per first-year +6%. The VP Finance advised that any effect on yield was expected to be small, based on the enrolment consultant's 2021 price-elasticity estimate. Admissions to be informed of the new award amounts before early-action decisions are released.

catalogue.title: Yield by admission round (early action vs regular decision), Fall 2025 and Fall 2026 entering classes
catalogue.source: Office of Institutional Research extract, 12 Oct 2026
catalogue.text: Early action (decisions released 15 Dec in both years, legacy system): admits 2,300 → 2,380; enrolled 1,040 → 900; yield 45.2% → 37.8%. Regular decision (2026 processed on Quillstone): admits 2,820 → 2,890; enrolled 1,100 → 910; yield 39.0% → 31.5%. Share of admits who were merit-eligible (scored by the merit-review team): EA 54% in both years; RD 52% in both years. Median days from complete file to decision for merit-eligible files, 2026: EA 16, RD 38. IR note: early-action admits received their decisions and award letters on the prior-year timetable.

catalogue.title: Admits, enrolments and award amounts by scholarship tier, Fall 2025 and Fall 2026 entering classes
catalogue.source: Joint Institutional Research and Financial Aid extract, 14 Oct 2026
catalogue.text: Tier eligibility criteria were the same in both years. Presidential (award $20,000 both years): admits 410 → 420; enrolled 150 → 152; yield 36.6% → 36.2%. Dean's ($14,000 → $9,000): admits 1,150 → 1,190; enrolled 520 → 380; yield 45.2% → 31.9%. Merit ($9,000 → $5,000): admits 1,560 → 1,610; enrolled 700 → 520; yield 44.9% → 32.3%. No merit award (need-based grants only or full pay; policy unchanged): admits 2,000 → 2,050; enrolled 770 → 758; yield 38.5% → 37.0%. Totals: admits 5,120 → 5,270; enrolled 2,140 → 1,810. The extract does not separate early-action and regular-decision admits.

catalogue.title: Survey of admitted students who did not enrol, spring 2026, with spring 2025 comparison
catalogue.source: Admissions Office survey of admits who declined or had not paid a deposit by 15 May
catalogue.text: Responses: 2025, n=540 (18% of non-enrolling admits); 2026, n=610 (18%). 'Most important reason for not enrolling' (one choice): cost or financial aid 39% → 46%; school closer to home 17% → 15%; academic programme 21% → 17%; slow or confusing communication from Admissions 8% → 13%; campus visit experience 6% → 5%; other 9% → 4%. Results are not broken out by admission round or award tier. Free-text comments include 'took forever to hear back' and 'the other offer was better.'

catalogue.title: Quillstone portal support ticket log, 6 Jan – 31 Mar 2026
catalogue.text: Applicants and counsellors opened 212 tickets. Categories: login or password 71; document shown as 'missing' or 'pending' 64; application fee payment 29; staff-side reading queue or scoring module 33; other 15. Of the 64 document-status tickets, 51 were closed as 'document present after status refresh'. The other 13 were auto-closed after 14 days with no resolution note. The export does not include applicant file contents or the time each file was marked complete.

catalogue.title: Vendor statement on the January 2026 portal go-live
catalogue.source: Statement from the Quillstone Systems account manager, 9 Oct 2026
catalogue.text: 'From go-live on 6 January the platform met its contracted availability target (99.6% measured, 99.5% required). We delivered the scholarship-scoring module three weeks after the original date because in December Marrowbridge changed the award amounts in its scoring rubric. Document status displays refresh on a cycle and can briefly show an upload as pending. In our experience, decision delays of this kind reflect client staffing levels rather than the software.'

catalogue.title: Merit-review queue and reader staffing records, Dec 2025 – Apr 2026
catalogue.text: Merit-review readers on staff: six until 19 Dec 2025 and four after that (two posts frozen under the hiring pause). Scoring module unavailable 8–16 Jan 2026 (vendor incident ticket QS-0412). Merit-review backlog: 410 files on 15 Jan, 1,880 on 9 Feb, 620 on 6 Mar, 0 on 27 Mar. Overtime logged by the merit team in Feb 2026: 212 hours. The records do not separate reader time spent waiting on the module from time spent scoring. There is no period with four readers on the legacy system to compare against.

catalogue.title: Regional projections of high-school graduates, 2024–2030
catalogue.source: State education department projections, published March 2026
catalogue.text: Public and private high-school graduates in the university's four main recruiting states: 412,300 (2024 actual); 409,800 (2025 actual); 407,100 (2026 projected); 391,500 (2030 projected). According to the projections, most of the decline comes after 2027, and college-going rates stay flat over the period.

catalogue.title: Published tuition and scholarship announcements of five competitor universities, 2026–27
catalogue.source: Compiled by the admissions marketing team from public websites, Sep 2026
catalogue.text: Covers the five universities that Marrowbridge admits most often name as alternatives. Published tuition for 2026–27 rose between 2.9% and 4.4% (Marrowbridge: 3.5%). None announced a new scholarship programme or a change to its published merit award amounts for 2026 entrants. Two expanded their honours colleges. The net prices actually offered to individual admits are not published.

catalogue.title: Admitted-student event registrations and attendance, spring 2025 and spring 2026
catalogue.text: In-person Admitted Student Day (April): 1,320 families attended in 2025 and 1,290 in 2026. Virtual admitted-student sessions: registrations 2,040 → 2,210. Overnight visit programme: 310 → 298 students. Event satisfaction score (1–5): 4.4 in both years. These records do not link attendance to admission round or award tier.

catalogue.title: Admissions Office operating and marketing budget, FY2025–FY2026
catalogue.text: Admissions operating budget: $4.82m in FY2025, $4.79m in FY2026. Recruitment travel and marketing: $1.21m → $1.18m. Purchased prospect lists: 92,000 → 95,000 names. Quillstone licence and implementation cost $0.64m in FY2026, replacing a legacy licence of $0.31m. The staffing budget was reduced by two frozen posts from December 2025.

catalogue.title: Enrolment deposit portal availability and transaction log, 1 Apr – 5 May 2026
catalogue.source: Quillstone deposit module logs, with 2025 legacy deposit page comparison
catalogue.text: Availability 99.9%, with one 40-minute outage on 22 Apr (14:10–14:50). Deposit transactions attempted: 1,904; completed: 1,881; failed: 23, of which 19 were retried successfully within 24 hours. Prior-year legacy deposit page: 2,237 attempted, 2,209 completed. Help-desk calls about deposits: 37 (2025: 41).

catalogue.title: Internal audit report on the Admissions Office, 2023
catalogue.text: Scope: applicant data retention, fee-waiver approvals, and user access to the legacy admissions system. Findings: three medium-risk issues. The retention schedule was not applied to 2017 files; fee-waiver approvals were undocumented in 6 of 40 samples; and two staff who had left still had active accounts. All three issues were marked closed by June 2024. The audit made no findings on decision timeliness or yield.

catalogue.title: Anonymous pulse survey of Admissions Office staff, March 2026
catalogue.source: HR pulse survey, 18–25 Mar 2026 (31 of 38 staff responded)
catalogue.text: 'I have the tools to do my job' (1–5): 3.9 in Mar 2025 → 2.6. 'My workload is manageable': 3.4 → 2.1. Comments: 'the scoring module freezes on every third file'; 'we're two readers short and nobody will say when the posts unfreeze'; 'families keep asking why their award is smaller than their older sibling's was'; 'we'll get blamed for whatever happens in May.'

catalogue.title: Interview notes, Director of Financial Aid, 8 Oct 2026
catalogue.source: Chief of staff's notes from an interview with Director of Financial Aid Marisol Dunne
catalogue.text: Merit awards are generated from the admissions tier and printed on the admission letter. Financial Aid applies whatever amounts the finance committee sets. Need-based packages went out on 1 March for early action and 1 April for regular decision, the same dates as in 2025. Award appeals rose from about 150 to 'roughly 400'. Dunne says the office logs appeals by date, not by tier or outcome, and she 'couldn't tell you who appealed and then came anyway.'

catalogue.title: First-year net tuition revenue report, Fall 2026 census
catalogue.text: Published tuition: $41,200 (+3.5%). Net tuition per enrolled first-year (after all institutional aid): $22,950 in Fall 2025 → $24,310 in Fall 2026 (+5.9%). Total first-year net tuition: $49.1m → $44.0m (−10.4%). First-year institutional discount rate: 47% → 41%. The report does not break out revenue or aid by award tier or admission round.

hypotheses.text: Slower regular-decision turnaround after the January move to the new application portal lowered the share of admitted students who enrolled.
The revised merit scholarship schedule for Fall 2026 entrants lowered the share of admitted students who enrolled.
A smaller or academically weaker applicant pool reduced the number of first-year students the university could enrol.
The new application portal failed to record some documents that applicants had submitted.
A general softening in demand, affecting all groups of admitted students alike, lowered the share of admitted students who enrolled.

edges.from: Slower regular-decision turnaround after the January portal migration
edges.to: Fall in yield among admitted students

edges.from: Revised merit scholarship schedule for Fall 2026 entrants
edges.to: Fall in yield among admitted students

edges.from: Two merit-review reader posts frozen in December 2025
A smaller or academically weaker applicant pool

actions.text: Replace the Director of Admissions before the next recruitment cycle, citing the enrolment shortfall.

Take the merit scholarship schedule back to the finance committee with a proposal to restore award levels in the tiers whose yield fell, with the net-revenue trade-off modelled, before next cycle's award letters go out.
Set a decision-turnaround target for next cycle's regular-decision files and have Admissions report progress against it to the provost each month.
Instruct the portal vendor to rebuild the document-upload module under the contract's remediation clause before the next cycle opens.
